title: Council receives 2024 budget under new provincial process
subtitle: Ward 10 council vacancy declared, off-street parking by-law changes, and regional budget updates on the food bank and A Better Tent City.
overview: Council received the Mayor's proposed 2024 Budget and directed staff to implement it {{vote:m1}}. Under the new provincial process, the budget is treated as adopted when no amendments are submitted, and none were. Council still held a vote to keep the process collaborative. The budget includes $1.6 million for strategic initiatives: traffic calming and trail connections, an arena energy strategy, two more playground replacements, a newcomers strategy, better access to the Cameron Heights Pool, and a city-wide data strategy.

Capital projects that one councillor had a declared conflict on were voted on separately {{vote:m2}}. Council also declared the Ward 10 councillor seat vacant and asked the City Clerk to report on ways to fill it at a January 8, 2024 Special Council meeting {{vote:m3}}. Council passed by-laws amending the off-street parking by-law as well.

The Mayor reported that Regional Council approved its 2024 budget with a 6.9% tax increase. The Region doubled its food bank contribution and funded A Better Tent City for the next two years. Because the City collects taxes for the Region and school boards, residents may see changes in how tax bills show each share.

decisions.detail: Council received the Mayor's proposed 2024 Budget and directed staff to implement it, apart from the capital projects voted on separately {{vote:m1}}.

Council separately received and approved implementation of three capital projects (the Mill Courtland Community Centre and Rockway Centre redevelopment, Franklin Street reconstruction, and First Street) on a recorded vote {{vote:m2}}.
Council declared the Ward 10 councillor office vacant and directed the City Clerk to report on methods to fill it by the January 8, 2024 Special Council meeting.
Council gave third reading to three by-laws amending Schedules A, B and C of the municipal off-street parking by-law.

debate: Councillors who spoke in favour said the budget kept the tax increase below the two-year inflation average while maintaining services and adding priorities. They credited staff discipline and the strategic plan.
Several councillors noted that no amendments were submitted. They saw this as a sign of the collaborative approach, and one said the Mayor did not need to use strong mayor powers.

The Mayor said the new provincial process is not one the Mayor favours, but that Council and staff worked to keep it as close to past practice as possible. Council was receiving the budget and directing its implementation, not approving it.

One councillor said they had been on leave in November and could not speak or ask questions at the December 4 presentation. They said they would not support the motion, and that declining to vote is recorded as a vote against.

After the regional budget update, one councillor asked that tax information show the City, Region and school board shares separately. Staff nodded in agreement and said they would work with communications on it.
